passages.t: ‘The LORD reigns’: above the roar of many waters
passages.happening:
Psalm 93 is short and has no heading. It opens with a shout: “The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty; the LORD has clothed and armed Himself with strength” (verse 1). Because he reigns, “The world indeed is firmly established; it cannot be moved” (verse 1). “Your throne was established long ago; You are from all eternity” (verse 2).

Then comes a picture of water. “The floodwaters have risen, O LORD; the rivers have raised their voice; the seas lift up their pounding waves” (verse 3). Each line gets louder.

But the LORD is greater. Above the roar of the waters and the breakers of the sea, “the LORD on high is majestic” (verse 4).

It ends quietly. “Your testimonies are fully confirmed; holiness adorns Your house, O LORD, for all the days to come” (verse 5).
passages.hearers:
‘The LORD reigns’ is the cry of a coronation. When a king was crowned, the people shouted that he was king. Here the cry is for God. Psalm 93 is the first of several psalms in Book Four that sing that the LORD is King (93 and 95 to 99). The book page notes how this theme answers the loss of Israel's own kings at the end of Psalm 89.

The Mishnah lists Psalm 93 as the song the Levites sang in the temple on the sixth day of the week.

Israel's neighbours told stories of a storm god who fought the sea and was crowned king after he won. The note on Psalm 74 says more. Psalm 93 uses the same kind of picture, the waters lifting their voice. But there is no battle at all. The sea roars, and the LORD is simply higher. The sea is something he made, not a rival god.

Notice the last verse. After the thunder of the waves, the psalm turns to God's ‘testimonies’, his words, and to holiness in his house. God's strength and God's word go together.
passages.later:
When a storm hit the boat, Jesus “got up and rebuked the wind and the sea” (Mark 4:39). The disciples asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?” (Mark 4:41).

In Revelation, John hears a sound “like the rushing of many waters”, crying, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns” (Revelation 19:6).
passages.asks:
What floods are roaring in your life right now? Psalm 93 does not say the waters are quiet. It says they are loud, and that God is higher still.

Say the first line aloud when you are afraid: ‘The LORD reigns.’ It is not a feeling. It is a fact you can stand on while the waves are still pounding.
